item.title: Ukraine strikes Russian retail giant
item.description:
Ukrainian media reported that Ukrainian drones hit a logistics complex of the Russian retail giant Wildberries in the Tambov region.
The company's facilities in the region have been hit in previous Ukrainian strikes.

item.description: There are four languages of the redemption promised by Hashem, - for which, the four glasses of wine are drunk at the Seder - but there is a fifth promise as well. Which promise is that?

item.title: Man arrested for bringing guillotine to Capitol Hill
item.description:
Capitol Police in Washington, D.C., arrested a 35-year-old man from California after a guillotine was found in the bed of his pickup truck. Police said the truck was illegally parked near the Capitol complex.
According to authorities, the man was traveling from California to Washington, and investigators are looking into why he came to the city and what he intened to do with the guillotine. He was arrested on suspicion of possessing a dangerous weapon.

item.title: US temporarily freezes visa appointments at embassies worldwide
item.description:
The administration of US President Donald Trump has ordered a temporary freeze on visa appointments at US embassies and consulates around the world. The State Department said the move is intended to allow for a global training program for consular employees, aimed at improving screening and ensuring uniform evaluation of visa applicants, including regarding the possibility that they may become dependent on welfare benefits and public assistance in the United States.
According to the Financial Times, immigrant visa applicants who had already been scheduled for interviews received notices that their appointments had been postponed and were told that a new date would be set at a later time. At this stage, no timetable has been provided for the resumption of appointments.

item.description: Montreal city council approves a revised Middle East motion, removing calls to cut ties with Israel and accusations of “genocide" and “apartheid."

item.title: Trump sends Saudi nuclear deal to Congress, ties pact to Israel normalization
item.description: Trump sends Congress the Saudi civil nuclear deal, but says the pact will only proceed if Riyadh joins the Abraham Accords and normalizes ties with Israel.

item.description: Federal prosecutors seek to detain Larry Montes, accused of attacking worshippers and a security guard during services at New York's Central Synagogue.

item.description: Trump-endorsed Sen. Darline Graham wins the GOP Senate nomination in South Carolina and will face Democrat Annie Andrews in November.

item.title: Toronto police investigate alleged antisemitic incident in North York
item.description: Toronto police are investigating an alleged antisemitic incident near Bathurst and Sheppard, an area which has seen frequent anti-Israel demonstrations.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s representatives: She died after a brief battle with cancer
item.description:
Representatives for country music legend Dolly Parton, who died Tuesday at the age of 80, said she passed away following a “brief battle with cancer." Parton died at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville, surrounded by her family.
The type of cancer she had was not disclosed.

item.title: FBI arrests Ohio man accused of threatening Rep. Randy Fine and Trump
item.description: Ohio man arrested after allegedly sending a death threat against Rep. Randy Fine and calling for President Trump’s death.

item.title: Man moderately injured in violent incident in Haifa
item.description:
A 37-year-old man was moderately injured in a violent incident in Haifa.
Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics treated him at the scene and evacuated him to Bnei Zion Hospital in the city.

item.title: Iran vows Strait of Hormuz will remain closed, warns of preemptive action
item.description: Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister says the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until key conditions are met.

item.title: Reports: IDF carries out strikes in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Lebanese media reported that the IDF carried out a strike overnight in Kfar Rumman, in the Nabatieh Governorate of southern Lebanon.
Additional IDF strikes were also reported in Ali al-Taher, Al-Mansouri, Zar'bin and Al-Qantara.

item.title: Report: Rubio tells allies US is not planning new Iran strikes 'for the time being'
item.description: Axios reports Secretary of State Marco Rubio has told allies the US is not planning new Iran strikes for now, as Washington intensifies sanctions and economic pressure.

item.title: Likud: Ballots from primary election in Be’er Ya’akov to be recounted
item.description:
The Likud party announced that, following a decision by the party’s election committee, headed by retired Judge Menachem Ne’eman, ballots from the Likud primary election in Be’er Ya’akov will be recounted.
“The results will be incorporated into the final results after the appeals are heard this coming Thursday. Likud is committed to ensuring the integrity of the election process and adhering to the directives of the party’s tribunal and election committee," the party said in a statement.

item.title: Secret Service investigating Iranian video targeting Barron Trump
item.description: The Secret Service says it is investigating an Iranian state media video threatening Barron Trump and claiming his movements had been monitored.

item.title: Yair Netanyahu to Winter’s candidates: You’ll waste votes
item.description: The Prime Minister’s son personally addresses each candidate on Ofer Winter’s slate, warning that further fragmentation of the national camp could help the left-wing bloc.

item.title: New report reveals: How PA schools celebrated the October 7 massacre
item.description: A special report presents quotes from ceremonies, assemblies, and events held in Palestinian Authority schools honoring the heroism of Hamas terrorists on the day of the October 7 massacre.

item.description: Leket Israel CEO Joseph Gitler discusses rescuing surplus food, supporting Israeli farmers and expanding food assistance ahead of Rosh Hashanah, with a goal of distributing more than 700,000 meals to people in need.
